# The Lantern Road

Mara woke before the bells. Pale light pooled on the sill, and the room smelled of tar and cold ash. She dressed in the dark, fumbling with the buttons of a coat that had belonged to her father.

Aldric waited in the yard beside the well, a lantern hanging from his fist.

"You are late," he said.

"The road does not care," Mara answered. "It will be there when the sun is."

He laughed, a short sound that rang against the stones. Then he handed her a loaf, still warm, and she tore off the heel while the lantern swung between them.

They walked. Past the customs house, where Bellmere kept his ledgers, past the shuttered bakery and the fountain with its dry basin, the lane narrowed and climbed toward the ridge.

"Do you think he knows?" Mara asked.

"Bellmere hears everything," Aldric said. "Whether he cares is another matter."

At the top of the rise the town fell away. Mist lay over the valley like spilled milk, and a single bell tolled somewhere below.

# The Salt Market

By noon the square had filled with carts. Fishwives shouted prices over the creak of axles, and a boy darted between the stalls with a tray of warm pastries balanced on his head.

Mara bought a twist of salt and a length of cord. Aldric stood watching the crowd, his thumbs hooked in his belt.

"Someone is following us," he said.

She did not turn around. "Tall? Green scarf?"

"That one."

They lingered at a stall of copper pans until the stranger drifted closer. Then Aldric stepped out, quick as a cat, and caught the man's sleeve.

The man held up empty hands. A coin glinted between his fingers, and his grin was crooked.

"Bellmere sent me," he said. "He wants you both at the customs house before the tide turns."
